title: Unbounded projection formula for a closed immersion
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the unbounded structure-module derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback], derived direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. The functor $i_*$ on all structure-module sheaves is exact, so $Ri_*$ is computed by applying $i_*$ termwise to any representative complex. For every $E\in D(\mathcal O_Z)$ and $Q\in D(\mathcal O_P)$ the canonical projection-formula morphism is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_P)$:
$$Ri_*E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_P}Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_*(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_Z}Li^*Q).$$
No quasi-coherence, cohomological boundedness or Tor-dimension assumption on $E$ or $Q$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0B55, lemma-projection-formula-closed-immersion, including the exactness assertion in its proof.

proof.text: The underlying map of $i$ identifies $Z$ homeomorphically with a closed subset of $P$. The underlying abelian-sheaf pushforward is exact by [lem-sc-closed-immersion-pushforward-exact]. Forgetting module structure is faithful and preserves kernels and cokernels by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], so it reflects exactness: the homology module of a pushed-forward short exact sequence has zero underlying abelian sheaf and is zero. Thus $i_*$ is exact on all structure-module sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]: every complex computes $Ri_*$, with the canonical comparison $i_*A^\bullet\to Ri_*(A^\bullet)$ an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0B55, first two sentences; Modules Tag 01AX; Sites Modules Tag 03DA; Derived Categories Tag 015F

proof.text:
Choose a complex $A^\bullet$ representing $E$, and a K-flat resolution $K^\bullet\to Q_0^\bullet$ of any complex representing $Q$, using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the site of opens of $P$. By [def-pc-derived-pullback] and [lem-pc-kflat-pullback-preservation], $i^*K^\bullet$ represents $Li^*Q$ and is K-flat over $\mathcal O_Z$. Hence, by [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure] and step 1, the source and target of the required map are represented respectively by
$$L^\bullet=\operatorname{Tot}(i_*A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O_P}K^\bullet),\qquad R^\bullet=i_*\operatorname{Tot}(A^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O_Z}i^*K^\bullet).$$
For the target, $A^\bullet$ need not be K-flat: choose a K-flat resolution $c:A'^\bullet\to A^\bullet$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; the cone of $\operatorname{Tot}(c\otimes1):\operatorname{Tot}(A'^\bullet\otimes i^*K^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}(A^\bullet\otimes i^*K^\bullet)$ is $\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Cone}(c)\otimes i^*K^\bullet)$, acyclic because $\operatorname{Cone}(c)$ is acyclic and $i^*K^\bullet$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. So the derived tensor of the K-flat pair $(A'^\bullet,i^*K^\bullet)$ is represented by $\operatorname{Tot}(A^\bullet\otimes i^*K^\bullet)$ through this quasi-isomorphism; the source is treated by the same cone argument in step 6. These are direct-sum total complexes; no boundedness or quasi-coherence has been used.

For module sheaves $M$ on $Z$ and $N$ on $P$, form the ordinary projection morphism $m_{M,N}:i_*M\otimes_{\mathcal O_P}N\to i_*(M\otimes_{\mathcal O_Z}i^*N)$. On sections it sends $s\otimes t$ to $s\otimes i^*t$. This is balanced over $\mathcal O_P$, commutes with restriction, and therefore gives a map from the sheafified tensor presheaf [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Equivalently it is the transpose under [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] of the tensor pullback map followed by the ordinary counit. At $p\notin i(Z)$ both stalks vanish by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks] and [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-tensor]. At $p=i(z)$, these nodes and [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] identify its stalk with
$$M_z\otimes_{\mathcal O_{P,p}}N_p\longrightarrow M_z\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Z,z}}(N_p\otimes_{\mathcal O_{P,p}}\mathcal O_{Z,z}),\qquad u\otimes v\longmapsto u\otimes(v\otimes1).$$
The inverse sends $u\otimes(v\otimes b)$ to $bu\otimes v$. The tensor balancing relations make it well defined and the two composites are the identity. The same section formula proves naturality separately in $M$ and $N$.

A module-sheaf map whose stalks are bijective is an isomorphism: apply [lem-sc-abelian-sheaf-mono-iff-stalk-mono] and [lem-sc-abelian-sheaf-epi-iff-stalk-epi] after forgetting modules, and use [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] to detect zero kernel and cokernel. Thus every $m_{M,N}$ in step 3 is invertible. Also $i_*$ commutes with arbitrary set-indexed direct sums of module sheaves. Indeed, consider the canonical comparison $\bigoplus_a i_*M_a\to i_*(\bigoplus_aM_a)$. By [lem-pc-stalk-direct-sums] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks], on an image stalk it is the identity on $\bigoplus_a(M_a)_z$; off the image both sides are zero. The same stalk detection makes the comparison invertible. This includes the empty family.

source.place: Tag 0B55, direct-sum and stalk argument; Sheaves Tags 007S, 00AE and Section 009E(5); Modules Tag 01AZ

proof.text: In total degree $n$, apply $m_{A^p,K^q}$ on every summand with $p+q=n$, and then the inverse of the direct-sum comparison from step 4. This gives a degreewise isomorphism $m^\bullet:L^\bullet\to R^\bullet$. Naturality of $m$ in its first variable makes it commute with $d_A\otimes1$, and naturality in its second variable makes it commute with $1\otimes d_K$. On the summand $(p,q)$ the latter differential carries the same factor $(-1)^p$ on both sides, by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Therefore $m^\bullet$ is a chain isomorphism. This proves the required isomorphism on the representative complexes once its canonical-map identification is checked.

To check that identification, choose a K-flat resolution $a:B^\bullet\to i_*A^\bullet$ on $P$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Since $K^\bullet$ is K-flat, $\operatorname{Tot}(a\otimes1)$ is a quasi-isomorphism: its cone is $\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Cone}(a)\otimes K^\bullet)$, acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Also $\operatorname{Tot}(B^\bullet\otimes K^\bullet)$ is K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-tensor-product]. First, the isomorphism $e(P)$ of [lem-pc-kflat-pullback-adjunction-comparison] is inverse to the left-derived counit $\epsilon_i(P)$ used in [def-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-comparison], for every K-flat $P$: apply that lemma to $I=i^*P$ and to the termwise unit $\eta_P:P\to i_*i^*P$ of [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction], whose ordinary transpose is the identity; this gives $e(P)^{-1}=\mathrm{homEquiv}^{-1}(Q(\eta_P)\circ\text{direct-image comparison})$, which is $\epsilon_i(P)$ because the derived adjunction of [def-pc-relative-mv-maps] is pinned to the left-derived counit and the right-derived unit. Write $\widetilde a:i^*B^\bullet\to A^\bullet$ for the ordinary adjoint of $a$. By [lem-pc-kflat-pullback-adjunction-comparison], its localization is the derived adjoint of the localization of $a$, followed by the canonical direct-image comparison; under $B^\bullet\simeq Ri_*E$ it is the derived counit at $E$. The defining K-flat equation of [def-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-comparison] says that the pullback tensor comparison on $(B^\bullet,K^\bullet)$ is represented by $i^*\operatorname{Tot}(B^\bullet\otimes K^\bullet)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(i^*B^\bullet\otimes i^*K^\bullet)$. Consequently the adjoint defining the projection map is represented by this chain isomorphism followed by $\operatorname{Tot}(\widetilde a\otimes1)$. Applying the same adjunction comparison to the K-flat source $\operatorname{Tot}(B^\bullet\otimes K^\bullet)$ identifies its derived transpose with the ordinary transpose. On each pure tensor of sections, that transpose is exactly $m^\bullet\circ\operatorname{Tot}(a\otimes1)$: both send $b\otimes k$ to $a(b)\otimes i^*k$. Thus the canonical projection morphism is the localization of $m^\bullet$, after inverting $\operatorname{Tot}(a\otimes1)$.

By step 5 the localized map $m^\bullet$ is invertible, and step 6 identifies it with the canonical projection-formula morphism. Together with step 1 this proves both assertions of the item for every $E$ and $Q$, including unbounded complexes and non-quasi-coherent cohomology.
